video_identity.title: Automating Game Mechanics Research & Visual Wiki Generation with Claude Code
video_identity.creator: Game Design Workflow / Claude Code Agent User
video_identity.subject: Automating action game mechanics documentation, research, and local visual wiki creation using AI coding agents.

access_observation.audio_used: Voiceover narration describing the purpose of building a mechanics master log, automating data gathering via Claude Code agent, and establishing a local visual wiki with video clips/GIFs.
access_observation.visuals_used: Google Sheets master log spreadsheet, VS Code terminal running Claude Code agent automation scripts, YouTube video reference clips, and a custom web-based local visual wiki for game characters.

episodes.observed_visual_fact: Displays a Google Sheets spreadsheet titled 'Mechanics Log' detailing character abilities, input commands, targeting types, core damage/CC effects, cooldowns, and video links across various games.
episodes.instructor_claim: The designer maintains a master log of game mechanics across many titles to capture research and reference for action game mechanics and ability kits.
episodes.interpretation: Structured tabular data allows quantitative analysis and systematic comparison of action mechanics across different games.
episodes.hypothesis: Standardizing game mechanics into categorized attributes helps designers recognize balance patterns and kit structures.
episodes.reference_workflow_stage: Data structuring and initial reference cataloging.
episodes.concrete_action: Maintained a Google Sheet tracking ability ranges, targeting logic, cooldowns, and visual links.
episodes.reason: To catalog action game mechanics into a centralized, comparable format.
episodes.failure_or_warning: Manual entry of deep mechanical data across dozens of games is highly labor-intensive and hard to maintain.
episodes.transferable_principle: Organize reference mechanics into standardized schema fields (range, target, cooldown, effect type) for clear comparative analysis.

episodes.observed_visual_fact: Opens a hyperlinked YouTube video showing Captain America's 'Freedom Charge' ability in Marvel Rivals with timestamped gameplay footage.
episodes.instructor_claim: Reference video clips are linked directly within the mechanics log for instant visual verification.
episodes.interpretation: Linking numerical metrics to video evidence provides concrete visual context for abstract stat values.
episodes.hypothesis: Direct video links reduce ambiguity between technical stat descriptions and visual execution.
episodes.concrete_action: Navigated from spreadsheet link to timestamped gameplay footage.
episodes.reason: To verify animation timing, area-of-effect visual footprints, and character movement dynamics.
episodes.failure_or_warning: External web links can become broken or lose timestamp sync if source videos are removed.
episodes.transferable_principle: Pair qualitative visual media directly with quantitative mechanical specifications.

episodes.observed_visual_fact: Shows VS Code editor running a Claude Code agent executing automated tasks like research, updating markdown files, generating GIFs, and calling external APIs.
episodes.instructor_claim: The research and logging process was automated using a Claude Code agent.
episodes.interpretation: CLI agents can perform autonomous web scraping, video asset downloading, GIF slicing, and database generation.
episodes.hypothesis: Automating reference gathering via AI agents eliminates tedious manual data entry and asset trimming.
episodes.concrete_action: Executed bash automation scripts via Claude Code agent to gather character data and generate media assets.
episodes.reason: To automate repetitive web searching, data parsing, and media cropping tasks.
episodes.failure_or_warning: High API token usage can occur during heavy batch scraping and text processing runs.
episodes.transferable_principle: Leverage agentic scripting to automate time-consuming reference gathering pipelines.

episodes.observed_visual_fact: Displays auto-populated spreadsheet rows updating across multiple games (e.g., Marvel Rivals, 2XKO fighting game guide footage).
episodes.instructor_claim: The agent populates sheets per game, attaching video timestamps and skill metadata.
episodes.interpretation: Multi-agent tasks can extract structured mechanical data from unstructured game guides and gameplay clips across different genres.
episodes.hypothesis: Cross-genre data ingestion provides broader design insights than staying within a single title type.
episodes.concrete_action: Ingested ability data and timestamp links across fighting games and hero shooters.
episodes.reason: To build a cross-genre catalog of action combat mechanics.
episodes.failure_or_warning: Inaccurate source guides or community wikis can propagate incorrect numbers into the master database.
episodes.transferable_principle: Apply uniform data structures across diverse genres to identify universal combat principles.

episodes.observed_visual_fact: Transitions to a locally hosted web application ('Marvel Rivals Visual Wiki') presenting character cards (Hulk, Venom, Thor) with automatically clipped gameplay GIFs, stat badges, and descriptions.
episodes.instructor_claim: A parallel agent builds a local visual wiki based on the spreadsheet data, clipping GIFs to present contents in an easy-to-navigate form.
episodes.interpretation: A visual wiki provides a superior user experience compared to raw spreadsheets for browsing combat animations and visual effects.
episodes.hypothesis: Interactive visual dashboards increase usability and adoption during active game design and art reviews.
episodes.reference_workflow_stage: Visual wiki generation and interactive review.
episodes.concrete_action: Rendered a web-based visual wiki dashboard featuring automated GIF previews and categorized ability tags.
episodes.reason: To make gameplay references visually intuitive and quickly browsable.
episodes.failure_or_warning: Auto-generated GIF clips may cut off key animation frames if timestamp boundaries are inaccurate.
episodes.transferable_principle: Transform flat tabular reference logs into interactive visual media hubs for rapid design evaluation.

episodes.observed_visual_fact: Browses Iron Man's character page in the visual wiki, clicking through media modals displaying playable video/GIF loops of Unibeam, Armor Overdrive, and Micro-Missile Barrage.
episodes.instructor_claim: The pipeline from concept to execution took less than a day, establishing a strong foundation that can be updated over time.
episodes.interpretation: Rapid automated prototyping of toolchains allows designers to create custom reference systems with low setup friction.
episodes.hypothesis: Having direct access to looped move animations alongside hit data accelerates 3D ability design and balance iteration.
episodes.concrete_action: Reviewed individual move animations (Iron Man Unibeam, Micro-Missiles) inside full-screen detail modals.
episodes.reason: To analyze specific animation timing, particle trajectories, and visual impact cues.
episodes.failure_or_warning: Initial token/api expenditure is high during initial project setup.
episodes.transferable_principle: Maintain local, interactive media playback systems alongside numerical parameters to streamline combat design decisions.

reference_categories: CLI Code Automation Scripts (Claude Code Agent Logs)
acquisition_methods: Web searching character wikis and official game databases
Automated scraping of video guides and timestamped media URLs
CLI agent processing for data extraction and formatting
Automatic video trimming and GIF conversion of move clips
organization_methods: Tabular spreadsheet columns organized by Skill, Input, TAB Type, Targeting, Range, Core Effects, Cooldown, and Link
Character-level tagging by role (e.g., Vanguard, Duelist, Strategist)
Grid-based visual character selector in a local web application
Modal overlays pairing looped gameplay video with quantitative ability stats
selection_and_rejection_criteria: Retain abilities with clear mechanical descriptions, quantitative damage/cooldown values, and visual footage
Filter out unverified community claims or entries lacking video proof
Prioritize games with distinct, well-defined action combat mechanics (e.g., Hero Shooters, Fighting Games)
contradiction_handling: Cross-reference community guide numbers against primary video footage to ensure timestamp accuracy and patch validity.
iterative_research_triggers: Addition of new playable characters or balance patches in target games
Missing visual footage or timestamp misalignment in existing entries
Expansion of research scope into new game titles or genres
principles: Pair quantitative mechanics data directly with looping visual footage
Automate repetitive reference collection using agentic code workflows
Structure cross-game data into uniform schemas to enable comparative design analysis
Build local, lightweight presentation layers (wikis/dashboards) to improve data usability during active design phases
limitations: This video demonstrates documentation workflow tooling rather than hands-on 3D mesh modeling or sculpting.
High initial token consumption for LLM code agents during batch extraction.
Automated web scraping is susceptible to breaking when source website structures or YouTube link formats change.
claims_requiring_external_verification: The claim that the complete pipeline from concept to working visual wiki was executed in less than one day.
Accuracy of specific damage/cooldown numbers listed in the spreadsheet for Marvel Rivals and 2XKO.
proposed_experiments: Test the agent workflow on a new game genre (e.g., Souls-like action RPGs) to see if the schema fields adapt without structural changes.
Compare manual spreadsheet construction time versus automated agent-driven creation to quantify productivity gains and token costs.
